extracted.intended_audience: communications teams, PR professionals, and media relations practitioners producing broadcast-ready video assets
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, shooting, and packaging b-roll that supports broadcast public relations campaigns—covering strategic mapping to messages, legal clearances, technical specs, and editorial considerations to maximize pickup by TV outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of b-roll (reinforce narrative and context)
rubrics_metrics.description: B-roll isn’t filler; when used strategically, it reinforces the core narrative, adds context, and shapes how your audience perceives your brand, message, or public information campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use b-roll to strengthen storytelling and transform content from static to compelling. Position visuals to support the spokesperson and narrative rather than distract from them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact within short broadcast windows (30–90 seconds)
rubrics_metrics.description: In broadcast PR, your message often needs to make an impact within 30 to 90 seconds; b-roll enables stations to cut between interviews and relevant visuals, keep audiences engaged, and provide editorial value that encourages outlets to run the segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan b-roll moments that can be cut into short segments and that quickly illustrate key points so producers can craft tight, compelling pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visuals increase retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewers are more likely to remember content when it’s paired with relevant visuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose imagery that directly supports main talking points to boost audience recall of the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support editorial integrity (avoid feeling promotional)
rubrics_metrics.description: B-roll allows stations to contextualize the message and create a segment that feels authentic, not promotional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide footage that helps reporters tell an editorial story—real moments, context, and impartial visuals—rather than staged advertorial shots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drive broadcast placement with professional visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence of professional, customizable visuals makes your story more usable and appealing to TV producers and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality, editable footage (varied shots, clean edits) increases the likelihood of pickup at both local and national outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: People-focused footage
rubrics_metrics.description: Clips of real people participating in events, using services, or offering testimonials add emotion and relatability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture candid or natural interactions to humanize the story; ensure consent/release forms for identifiable individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action-oriented visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Footage of a doctor administering a vaccine, a worker installing safety equipment, or volunteers in motion helps convey urgency or impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action shots communicate impact quickly—frame them so the activity is clear and visually compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual/environmental establishing shots
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing visuals like city streets, school entrances, or clinic exteriors help ground the story in a recognizable setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wide and medium contextual shots to set scene and provide geography or situational context for reporters and viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and process visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Animated graphs, diagrams, or over-the-shoulder shots of a person interacting with technology can simplify abstract concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, legible visualizations and process shots that can be used as cutaways to explain complex topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness, relevance, and alignment with key message
rubrics_metrics.description: The most effective footage is timely, relevant, and visually aligned with the campaign’s key message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize footage that directly illustrates the central talking points and is current to the campaign or event timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make footage usable without additional production
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective b-roll delivers content that stations can quickly incorporate without requiring additional production work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clean, standalone clips (no missing lead-ins or jarring edits) and file formats that are ready for editors to drop into segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map visuals to messages (message-to-shot mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each key talking point should have a corresponding visual moment. For example, if your spokesperson discusses community outreach, include shots of real interactions with the public to reinforce the message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During pre-production, create a shot list that ties each key point to 1–2 specific b-roll moments to ensure consistent narrative support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scout and secure locations early
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose dynamic but appropriate environments where your footage will be captured, whether in the field or a controlled studio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early scouting prevents surprises and ensures the location visually supports the story; consider background activity, light, access, and permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure legal clearance (signed releases and permissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Always secure signed releases for identifiable individuals and permissions for recognizable locations or branded elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal clearance is non-negotiable for media outlets—obtain written consent and location/branding permissions before shooting, especially for national distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution and format (technical spec)
rubrics_metrics.description: Always film in HD or higher (1080p minimum), and deliver files in formats preferred by media outlets (e.g., .mov, .mp4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow broadcaster format preferences; failing to meet resolution/format standards (1080p+) may result in rejection or reduced visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and pacing of clips
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a mix of 5- to 10-second clips with natural motion and no abrupt movements. Each should be clean and standalone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply varied-length clips but favor 5–10s usable cutaways; avoid abrupt edits or movements that make clips unusable for smooth cuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a tripod or gimbal for stability, avoid cluttered backgrounds, and follow standard framing conventions (e.g., rule of thirds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stable, well-composed shots look professional and are easier for editors to use. Avoid distracting elements in frame and ensure subject clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid disqualifiers (logos, copyrighted content, poor techniques)
rubrics_metrics.description: No logos, brand marks, or copyrighted content in the frame unless cleared. Avoid jump cuts, excessive zooms, or poor lighting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements can disqualify footage from use even if the content is otherwise broadcast-ready. Remove or clear branding beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide variety to support multiple platforms and segment types
rubrics_metrics.description: A diverse b-roll package should include different angles, scenes, and pacing to allow use across traditional broadcast, social media, and stakeholder presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shoot wide, medium, and tight versions of key moments; include social-friendly crop possibilities and audio-optional visuals for muted autoplay contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate b-roll with spokespeople and interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate interview content with supporting b-roll, allowing seamless transitions during broadcasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan interview soundbites with corresponding visual cutaways in mind so editors can match B-roll to quotes for coherent storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom editing and packaging (deliverable enhancements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble polished b-roll packages that include lower-thirds, graphic overlays, and captioning when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide optional pre-edited packages or templates that make it easier for newsrooms to use the footage while preserving editorial control; include captioning and basic graphics as required.
